commentary: A small gain, up £272, even though NVIDIA fell 4.3% to $166.19 (about −£143) after chief executive Jensen Huang resigned with immediate effect following reports of relationships with colleagues, one with a woman US officials suspect of links to Chinese intelligence. The shares had been down nearly 12% at the open before recovering. Finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO and the results are still due on 17 Nov. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq each lost 0.4% as energy shares rose. Alphabet gained 1.6% (about £165) as other chip firms rose, and the VWRP tracker added about £398 including the 116 units bought this week. The FTSE 100 rose 0.25% to 10,863.09 after UK growth in the third quarter was the fastest in two years. The gold fund fell 3.0% (about −£193) as gold dropped. The pound slipped to 1.3237 from 1.3277, which trims the US holdings in sterling.
